chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has intercourse with his wife while traveling during the month of Ramadan. He said: There is no harm in it. So do not see a contradiction between this report and the earlier reports, because the first report included the question about one who had intercourse with his wife during Ramadan, and he answered that there is no harm. It is not impossible that he did so out of ignorance, not knowing that it was not permissible for him. And he did not say in the report that it is permissible in every case. As for the last two hadiths and what is added to them from what has come in the books, it is not mentioned therein that he did so at night or during the day. It is not impossible that the permission came regarding the state of the night, not the day. And it can be understood, with acceptance, that they include mentioning the day for one upon whom desire overcomes and he cannot control himself and does not fear falling into the prohibited, so He granted him concession to attain from the permissible. And if it is the other case, it is as we have mentioned. And a report has been narrated that included mention of the day, and the explanation for it is what we have mentioned.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a traveler to have intercourse with his wife during the day in Ramadan?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents this narration from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah to resolve apparent contradictions in hadith regarding marital relations during the day in Ramadan for travelers. He argues that the permissibility applies specifically to those who are ignorant of the ruling or are overcome by desire and cannot control themselves, allowing them to consume the permissible (food) before the prohibited (intimacy), thereby reconciling the texts by distinguishing between the state of ignorance/necessity and general prohibition.
